title: A landslide with a length of 4 km (2.5 mi) occurs in Niscemi, Sicily, due to Storm Harry, prompting the evacuation of 1,500 residents.
text: A major landslide happened at the town of Niscemi, in Province of Caltanissetta, Sicily, Italy in 2026. A 4 km section of land collapsed, damaging buildings and infrastructure and causing the evacuation of over 1000 residents.

title: 6–22 February – The 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo.
text: The 2026 Winter Olympics, officially the XXV Olympic Winter Games and commonly known as Milano Cortina 2026, were an international winter multi-sport event held from 6 to 22 February 2026, at multiple sites across Lombardy, Veneto and Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol, with competition in selected events beginning on 4 February 2026. Featuring the debut of ski mountaineering as a Winter Olympic event, Milano Cortina 20…

title: Two skiers are killed in an avalanche along the Mont Blanc massif in Courmayeur.
text: The Mont Blanc massif is a mountain range in the Alps, located mostly in France and Italy, but also straddling Switzerland at its northeastern end. It contains eleven major independent summits, each over 4,000 metres (13,123 ft) in height.

title: An ambulance operator is arrested in Forlì after being accused of murdering five elderly patients between February and November 2025.
text: Forlì is a city and comune (municipality) in the region of Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy, and is, together with Cesena, the capital of the Province of Forlì-Cesena. With a population of 118,053 as of 2026, it is the 38th-largest city in Italy.

title: A magnitude 4.5 earthquake hits Sicily, damaging at least 600 homes in Ragalna.
text: Ragalna is a comune in the Metropolitan City of Catania in the Italian region Sicily, located about 150 kilometres (93 mi) southeast of Palermo and about 20 kilometres (12 mi) northwest of Catania. Points of interest include the Giardino Botanico "Nuova Gussonea", a botanical garden on Mount Etna.

title: The Italian Ministry of Defence states that Italy is to dispatch naval assets to Cyprus.
text: The Ministry of Defence is the government body of the Italian Republic responsible for military and civil defence matters and managing the Italian Armed Forces. It is led by the Italian Minister of Defence, a position occupied by Guido Crosetto since October 2022.

title: 6–15 March – The 2026 Winter Paralympics in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo.
text: The 2026 Winter Paralympics, also known as the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Paralympic Games, were the 14th edition of the Winter Paralympic Games, an international winter multi-sport parasports event governed by the International Paralympic Committee. It took place from 6 to 15 March at sites across Lombardy, Veneto and Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol, with competition in wheelchair curling beginning on 4 March.

title: The Constitutional Court of Italy rules in favour of the Meloni government's 2025 decree, which significantly restricted Italian citizenship by descent.
text: The Constitutional Court of the Italian Republic is the highest court of Italy in matters of constitutional law. Sometimes, the name Consulta is used as a metonym for it, because its sessions are held in Palazzo della Consulta in Rome.

title: An Italian MQ-9 Reaper is destroyed in an Iranian drone strike on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.
text: The General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper is a medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), one component of an Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS)) capable of either remotely controlled or autonomous flight operations, developed by General Atomics Aeronautical Systems (GA-ASI) primarily for the United States Air Force (USAF). The MQ-9 and other UAVs are referred to as Remotely Piloted Vehicles (RPVs) or Remotel…

title: Two people are killed in an avalanche at the Hohe Ferse near Ratschings.
text: Ratschings is a comune (municipality) in South Tyrol in northern Italy, located about 45 kilometres (28 mi) north of the city of Bolzano, on the border with Austria.

title: Three paintings by Auguste Renoir, Paul Cézanne and Henri Matisse are stolen in an overnight heist at the Magnani-Rocca Foundation near Parma. The paintings are recovered by police in August.
text: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a leading French Impressionist artist. In his depiction of feminine beauty, Renoir has been described as "the final representative of a tradition which runs directly from Rubens to Watteau." He was the father of the actor Pierre Renoir (1885–1952), the filmmaker Jean Renoir (1894–1979) and the ceramic artist Claude Renoir (1901–1969).

title: 22–23 March – 2026 Italian constitutional referendum: A proposal to reform the judiciary is rejected by 54% of voters.
text: A constitutional referendum concerning the reform of the judicial system was held in Italy on 22 and 23 March 2026. Its purpose was to revise Title II and Title IV of Part II of the Italian constitution.

title: Italy fails to qualify to the FIFA World Cup for a third consecutive time after losing to Bosnia and Herzegovina 4-1 on penalties at the 2026 FIFA World Cup qualification in Zenica.
text: The Italy national football team has represented Italy in men's international football since its first match in 1910. The team is controlled by the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), the governing body for football in Italy and a founding member of UEFA. Italy plays its home matches at various stadiums across the country, while its training center and technical headquarters, the Centro Tecnico Federale di Coverci…

title: Italy denies the United States Air Force the use the Sigonella base in Sicily for operations related to the war in Iran.
text: Naval Air Station Sigonella (IATA: NSY, ICAO: LICZ) is an Italian Air Force base (Italian: Aeroporto "Cosimo Di Palma" di Sigonella), and a U.S. Navy installation at Italian Air Force Base Sigonella in Lentini, Sicily, Italy. The whole NAS is a tenant of the Italian Air Force, which has the military and the administrative control.

title: Italy's Sal Da Vinci finishes fifth at Eurovision 2026 in Austria with the single "Per sempre sì".
text: Salvatore Michael Sorrentino, known professionally as Sal Da Vinci (Italian: ), is an American-born Italian singer, songwriter and actor, particularly known for his Neapolitan song repertory. As a songwriter, he has written for Ornella Vanoni and Renato Zero; he has also composed tracks with Gaetano Curreri, Pasquale Panella, and Roberto De Simone.

title: May–June – 2026 Italian local elections.
text: The 2026 Italian local elections were held on 24 and 25 May 2026, with runoffs in election being held on 7 and 8 June, in the ordinary-statute regions, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, and Sicily. In Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol, the elections were held on 17 May, with runoffs on 31 May.

title: Four migrant workers from Afghanistan and Pakistan are found killed inside a burnt-out minivan in Calabria.
text: Calabria is a region in Southern Italy. It is a peninsula bordered by the region Basilicata to the north, the Ionian Sea to the east, the Strait of Messina to the southwest, which separates it from Sicily, and the Tyrrhenian Sea to the west.

title: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni rejects claims by United States President Donald Trump that she had "begged" him for a photograph during the 52nd G7 summit in France. The remarks cause a diplomatic row, with Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani…
text: Giorgia Meloni is an Italian politician who has served as Prime Minister of Italy since October 2022. She is the first and only woman to hold the office and the head of the longest-serving government in the history of the Italian Republic.

title: Former Autostrade per l'Italia head Giovanni Castellucci is sentenced to 12 years' imprisonment for the Ponte Morandi collapse in 2018.
text: Autostrade per l'Italia S.p.A. is an Italian joint-stock company specializing in the management of motorway sections under concession and related maintenance activities. Originally established as a state-owned enterprise under the control of the IRI, it was privatized in 1999 and restructured into its current form in 2003.

title: Italy suspends Schengen Area agreements with Spain, citing the 2026 Morocco–Spain border incident.
text: In late July 2026, an estimated 80,000 people, mainly young men originating from Morocco, illegally breached and crossed the border from Morocco into the Spanish autonomous city of Ceuta in North Africa, with smaller numbers attempting to cross to Melilla, another Spanish autonomous city about 400 kilometres away along the Mediterranean coastline. This overwhelmed local reception facilities, and also prompted the …

title: A magnitude 4.7 earthquake hits Campania, injuring 26 people.
text: Campania is an administrative region of Italy, located in the south of the country; most of it is in the southwestern portion of the Italian Peninsula, but it also includes the small Phlegraean Islands – Ischia, Procida, Vivara, and Nisida – and the island of Capri. The capital is Naples.

title: Rafael Advanced Defense Systems' contract to run an anti-drone shield is cancelled by Rome Fiumicino Airport.
text: Rome Fiumicino Leonardo da Vinci International Airport (IATA: FCO, ICAO: LIRF) is an international airport in Fiumicino, Italy, serving Rome, its metropolitan area, Vatican City and the wider Lazio region. It is the busiest airport in the country, the eighth-busiest airport in Europe and the world's 40th-busiest airport with over 50 million passengers served in 2025.

title: Four Renaissance paintings attributed to Antonello da Messina are stolen in an overnight heist at the Regional Museum of Messina.
text: The Renaissance was a European period of history and cultural movement taking place at the end of the Late Middle Ages and the beginning of the early modern era. It is variously defined as covering the 15th and 16th centuries or, more broadly, as lasting from the 14th century to the 17th.

title: 21 August–6 September – 2026 Mediterranean Games in Taranto.
text: Taranto, historically also called Tarent in English, is a coastal city in Apulia, Southern Italy on the Gulf of Taranto. It is the capital of the province of Taranto, serving as an important commercial port as well as the main base of the Italian navy.

title: 9–26 September – 2026 Men's European Volleyball Championship in Bulgaria, Finland, Italy and Romania.
text: The 2026 Men's European Volleyball Championship, commonly referred to as EuroVolley Men 2026, was the 34th edition of the Men's European Volleyball Championship, a biennial international volleyball tournament organised by European Volleyball Confederation (CEV). The tournament took place from 9 to 26 September 2026 across Bulgaria, Finland, Italy, and Romania, marking the fourth consecutive time EuroVolley has bee…

title: Italy announces that it will deploy warships to protect shipping through the Bab al-Mandeb.
text: The Bab al-Mandab Strait, also written simply as the Bab al-Mandab or Bab el-Mandeb, is a strait and global chokepoint between Yemen on the Arabian Peninsula and Djibouti and Eritrea in the Horn of Africa, connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.

title: Prime Minister Meloni announces that the country would limit the number of foreign pupils per class and prohibit burqas and niqabs in schools.
text: A burqa, also known as harabah, is a type of enveloping outer garment worn by some Muslim women which fully covers the body and the face. The use of face veils has been documented in various ancient cultures, including the Byzantine Empire, Persia, and Arabia.

title: 24–27 September – 2026 Acrobatic Gymnastics World Championships in Pesaro.
text: Pesaro is a city and comune (municipality) in the region of Marche in Italy, capital of the province of Pesaro and Urbino, on the Adriatic Sea. With a population of 95,270 as of 2026, it is the 2nd-largest city in Marche, after Ancona, and the 50th-largest in Italy.

title: A court in Rome sentences three Egyptian security officials to ten years imprisonment for abducting Giulio Regeni.
text: Giulio Regeni was an Italian PhD student at the University of Cambridge who was kidnapped in Cairo, Egypt, on 25 January 2016, the fifth anniversary of the Tahrir Square protests, and found dead on 3 February near an Egyptian secret service prison.

title: Marchesi Antinori warehouse theft: Around 30,000 bottles of wine valued at €5 million are stolen in a heist at a storage facility owned by Antinori in Tuscany.
text: The Marchesi Antinori warehouse theft was a crime committed in early October 2026 in the Italian commune of Cortona. Having broken into the Marchesi Antinori wine warehouse , the criminals stole 30,000 bottles of wine with a total value of approximately € 5 million.

title: List of Italian submissions for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film
text: Italy has submitted films for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film since the conception of the award. The award is handed out annually by the United States Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences to a feature-length motion picture produced outside the United States that contains primarily non-English dialogue.
wiki: List of Italian submissions for the Academy Award for Best International Feature Film

title: “L'amore non mi basta” by Emma
text: "L'amore non mi basta" is a song recorded by Italian singer Emma. It was released on 11 October 2013 through Universal as the third single from her third studio album Schiena.

title: “Phantom” by Geolier featuring 50 Cent
text: "Phantom" is a song by Italian rapper Geolier with featured vocals by American rapper 50 Cent. It was released on 31 December 2025 by Atlantic Italy and Warner Music Italy as the third single from Geolier's fourth studio album, Tutto è possibile.

title: “End of Beginning” by Djo
text: "End of Beginning" is a song by the American actor and musician Joe Keery, under his stage name Djo. It was first made available by AWAL on September 16, 2022, as the sixth track from his second studio album, Decide.

title: “2 giorni di fila” by Geolier featuring Sfera Ebbasta and Anna
text: Gionata Boschetti, known professionally as Sfera Ebbasta (Italian: ), is an Italian rapper. He rose to prominence after the release of XDVR (2015), recorded with the collaboration of producer Charlie Charles and DEACC, which achieved commercial success in Italy.

title: “DTMF” by 7
text: "DTMF" is a song by Puerto Rican rapper Bad Bunny. It was released on January 23, 2025, as the fourth single from his sixth solo studio album Debí Tirar Más Fotos (2025).

title: “Male necessario” by 9
text: "Male necessario" is a song co-written and recorded by Italian rapper Fedez and Italian singer Marco Masini. It was released on 25 February 2026 through Warner Music Italy as the fourth single from Masini's thirteenth studio album, Perfetto imperfetto.

title: “Ossessione” by 10
text: "Ossessione" is a song co-written and recorded by Italian rapper Samurai Jay, released on 25 February 2026 through Island Records and Universal Music Italia. The song competed in the Sanremo Music Festival 2026.

title: “La testa gira” by Fred De Palma, Anitta and Emis Killa
text: "La testa gira" is a song by Italian singer Fred De Palma, Brazilian singer Anitta, and Italian rapper Emis Killa. It was released on 27 March 2026.
listen: La testa gira Fred De Palma, Anitta and Emis Killa

title: “Dai Dai” by 30
text: "Dai Dai" is a song by Colombian singer Shakira and Nigerian singer Burna Boy. It was released on 15 May 2026, through Ace Entertainment and Sony Music Latin as the official song for the 2026 FIFA World Cup held in the United States, Mexico, and Canada.

title: “Bugie” by 36
text: "Bugie" is a song by Italian rapper Shiva, released on 27 August 2026 by Milano Ovest and Sony Music, and included in the digital reissue of his seventh studio album, Vangelo. It was written by Shiva and produced by Drillionaire and Tommaso Torelli, known professionally as Toro2x.

title: “Per noi” by 38
text: "Per noi" is a song by Italian rapper Geolier, featuring Italian singer-songwriter Achille Lauro. It was released on 11 September 2026 as a single from the deluxe edition of Geolier's fourth studio album, Tutto è possibile.

title: “Lontano” by Sfera Ebbasta
text: "Lontano" is a song by Italian rapper Sfera Ebbasta. It was released on 22 September 2026 as the lead single from his seventh studio album, Purosangue.

title: “Non sei più tu” by Geolier featuring Lazza
text: Jacopo Lazzarini, known professionally as Lazza, is an Italian rapper and record producer.
listen: Non sei più tu Geolier featuring Lazza

title: Bulgaria adopts the euro, becoming the 21st member state of the eurozone.
text: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026, becoming the 21st member state of the eurozone. When Bulgaria joined the European Union in 2007 it committed to join the eurozone and replace its currency, the lev, with the euro.
wiki: Adoption of the euro in Bulgaria

title: Cyprus begins its role as President of the Council of the European Union.
text: The Council of the European Union, often referred to in the treaties and other official documents simply as the Council, and less formally known as the Council of Ministers, is the third of the seven institutions of the European Union as listed in the Treaty on European Union. It is one of two legislative bodies and together with the European Parliament serves to amend and approve, or veto, the proposals of the Eu…

title: 41 people are killed and 116 injured in a fire at a bar in Crans-Montana, Switzerland.
text: On 1 January 2026 at 01:26, during New Year celebrations, a fire broke out at Le Constellation bar in the ski-resort town of Crans-Montana, Valais, Switzerland. Forty-one people died in the fire, and 115 others were injured, with 83 initially being treated for severe burns.

title: The United States launches several airstrikes on multiple locations across northern Venezuela, capturing Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and first lady Cilia Flores.
text: On 3 January 2026, the United States launched a military strike in Venezuela and captured incumbent Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores. The US operation, codenamed Operation Absolute Resolve, began around 2 a.m.

title: Delcy Rodríguez is formally sworn in as the acting president of Venezuela after the capture of Nicolás Maduro.
text: Delcy Eloína Rodríguez Gómez is a Venezuelan lawyer, politician, and diplomat who has been the interim president of Venezuela since 2026, following the kidnapping of Nicolás Maduro during the U.S. occupation of Venezuela. She is the first woman in Venezuelan history to perform the duties of the presidency.

title: Fighting between Syrian government forces and the Kurdish armed group Syrian Democratic Forces begins.
text: On 13 January 2026, the Syrian transitional government launched an offensive against the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces in the territories of the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (DAANES). Initially focused on eastern Aleppo, around the towns of Deir Hafer and Maskanah, the offensive expanded on 17 January to the governorates of Raqqa, Deir ez-Zor and Al-Hasakah.

title: The United States seizes two shadow fleet tankers, including one under a Russian flag, in the United States oil blockade during Operation Southern Spear.
text: The Russian shadow fleet is a clandestine network of hundreds of vessels operated by Russia to evade sanctions, following the enactment of 2022 Russian crude oil price cap sanctions by the G7 countries and European Union, in response to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine. To circumvent these restrictions, vessels use complex ownership and corporate management structures, flags of convenience, and frequently chan…

title: Thongloun Sisoulith is re-elected as the General Secretary of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party at the 12th Central Committee's first meeting.
text: Thongloun Sisoulith is a Laotian politician and historian who serves as the general secretary of the Lao People's Revolutionary Party and the seventh president of Laos since 2021. Thongloun was born and educated in Houaphanh province, before receiving education in Leningrad and Moscow in the Soviet Union.

title: January 8–9 – Iran retaliates against nationwide protests, with tens of thousands reportedly killed on the 8th and 9th alone, and many thousands more detained amid a severe government crackdown.
text: The 2025–2026 Iranian protests were a series of nationwide demonstrations against the government of Iran that began on 28 December 2025 amid a deepening economic crisis. The unrest followed a sharp depreciation of the Iranian rial, rising inflation, and widespread shortages linked to international sanctions and government mismanagement.

title: 2025–2026 Southern Yemen campaign: The Southern Transitional Council announces its dissolution following territorial losses, including its capital Aden.
text: On 2 December 2025, during the Yemeni civil war, the Southern Transitional Council—a secessionist faction backed by the United Arab Emirates—launched a large-scale military offensive across southern Yemen, breaking years of military stalemate in the conflict. The operation began in the Hadhramaut Governorate, which at the time was under the control of the internationally recognized, Saudi-backed government of Yemen.

title: The 2026 Beninese parliamentary election is held.
text: Parliamentary elections were held in Benin on 11 January 2026 to elect all 109 members of the National Assembly. The preliminary results of the election were announced on 17 January.

title: Operation Arctic Endurance is launched by Denmark, with multiple European countries sending troops to Greenland in response to US President Donald Trump's threats of invasion or annexation of the island.
text: Donald John Trump is an American politician, media personality, and businessman who is the 47th president of the United States. A member of the Republican Party, he served as the 45th president from 2017 to 2021.

title: 2026 Ugandan general election: Incumbent President Yoweri Museveni wins reelection amidst protests over allegations of election fraud, leading to deaths of dozens of protestors and the abduction of main opposition candidate Bobi Wine.
text: General elections were held in Uganda on 15 January 2026 to elect the President and the Parliament. The elections were violent and disputed, with the US senate calling it a 'hollow exercise' and Human Rights Watch stating they 'were marred by human rights abuses'.

title: A fire at a shopping mall in Karachi, Pakistan, kills 80 people.
text: On 17 January 2026, a fire at the Gul Plaza shopping mall in Karachi, Pakistan, killed 80 people and injured over 20. The fire started after an unattended child accidentally set some artificial flowers alight with a matchstick in a shop on the ground floor.

title: 46 people are killed and 292 are injured after two trains derail in Adamuz in southern Spain.
text: On 18 January 2026, an Iryo high-speed train derailed in the municipality of Adamuz, in the province of Córdoba, Spain. A second train, Renfe Alvia 2384, crashed into it and was also derailed.

title: The 56th World Economic Forum begins in Davos, Switzerland.
text: The 56th World Economic Forum, also known as Davos 2026, was held from 19 to 23 January 2026 in Davos, Switzerland. Occurring at a time of heightened tensions between the United States and its NATO allies, including Canada, Greenland, and Europe, especially over the Greenland crisis, there were major speeches by world leaders including Mark Carney, Ursula von der Leyen and Donald Trump.

title: Islamic State insurgency in Afghanistan: Seven people are killed and twenty others injured in a bombing at a Chinese restaurant in Shahr-e Naw, Kabul, Afghanistan. The Islamic State – Khorasan Province claims responsibility.
text: The Islamic State is waging an ongoing insurgency against the Taliban regime in Afghanistan. The conflict initially began when both operated as rival insurgent groups in Nangarhar; since the formation of the Taliban's state in 2021, IS members have enacted a campaign of terrorism targeting both civilians and assassinating Taliban members using hit-and-run tactics.

title: The Syrian transitional government captures most of the territory held by the Syrian Democratic Forces following an offensive and subsequent ceasefire.
text: The Syrian transitional government, or the Ahmed al-Sharaa government, is the current provisional government of Syria. It was established on 29 March 2025 under President Ahmed al-Sharaa and is set to serve for a five-year transitional period under the Constitutional Declaration, which establishes a presidential system.

title: The United States officially leaves the World Health Organization.
text: The World Health Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations (UN) which coordinates responses to international public health issues and emergencies. It is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, and has six regional offices and 150 field offices worldwide.

title: Tô Lâm is re-elected as the General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam at the 14th National Congress.
text: Tô Lâm is a Vietnamese politician and former police officer who since 2024 has served as the general secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam (CPV), the highest-ranked position of the Vietnamese politics, and as the current President of Vietnam since 2026. He previously served as president from May to October 2024.

title: Iliana Iotova becomes the first female President of Bulgaria after the resignation of Rumen Radev.
text: Iliana Malinova Iotova is a Bulgarian politician and journalist who has served as president of Bulgaria since 23 January 2026. She is the first woman to hold the office.

title: Researchers operating China's Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) report the first experimental verification of a theorised density-free plasma operating regime, achieving stable electron densities approximately 1.3–1.65…
text: The Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak, also known as HT-7U (Hefei Tokamak 7 Upgrade), is an experimental superconducting tokamak magnetic fusion energy reactor in Hefei, China. Operated by the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science conducting its experiments for the Chinese Academy of Sciences, EAST began its operations in 2006.

title: Researchers at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology report a photo-Hall (Hall effect)–based method for detecting semiconductor electronic trap states with approximately 1,000-fold greater sensitivity than existing…
text: The Hall effect is the production of a potential difference, across an electrical conductor, that is transverse to an electric current in the conductor and to an applied magnetic field perpendicular to the current. Such potential difference is known as the Hall voltage.

title: Researchers at the Vienna University of Technology and the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology demonstrate self-sustained superradiant microwave emission, produced by interacting spins in diamond, offering potential applications in…
text: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology is a private, interdisciplinary graduate school located in Onna, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan.
wiki: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology

title: Astronomers using data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory report that 2025 MN45 has the fastest spin of any known asteroid larger than 0.5 km (0.31 mi) in diameter, completing one rotation every 1.88 minutes.
text: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory, formerly the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope, is an astronomical observatory in Coquimbo Region, Chile. Its main task is to conduct an astronomical survey of the southern sky every few nights, creating a ten-year time-lapse record, termed the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (also abbreviated LSST).

title: Paleoanthropologists publish a complete analysis of KNM-ER 64061, the most complete known skeleton of Homo habilis, discovered in 2012 in Kenya.
text: Homo habilis is an extinct species of archaic human from the Early Pleistocene of East and South Africa about 2.4 million years ago to 1.65 million years ago (mya).

title: Researchers report the discovery of a new quantum state, bridging the gap between quantum criticality and quantum topology via semimetal CeRu4Sn6.
text: In quantum physics, a quantum state is a mathematical entity that represents a physical system. Quantum mechanics specifies the construction, evolution, and measurement of a quantum state.

title: Researchers led by the University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences report the first direct experimental observation of the Migdal effect, a quantum process in which a recoiling atomic nucleus ejects an electron, confirming a prediction…
text: The University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences is a public university headquartered in Shijingshan, Beijing, China. It is owned by the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
wiki: University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: Researchers from the University of Copenhagen publish a Nature paper explaining little red dots as young and relatively small supermassive black holes enshrouded in a dense cocoon of ionized gas.
text: Nature is a British weekly international scientific journal publishing peer-reviewed research across the natural sciences, including biology, physics, chemistry, the earth sciences, and related interdisciplinary fields. It operates editorial offices in London, the United States, continental Europe, and Asia under the international scientific publishing company Springer Nature.

title: Michelangelo's preparatory sketch of a foot for The Libyan Sibyl is sold at Christie’s for $27.2 million including fees.
text: Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni, known mononymously as Michelangelo, was an Italian sculptor, painter, architect, and poet of the High Renaissance. He was born in the Republic of Florence but was mostly active in Rome from his 30s onwards.

title: The Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam announces the retrieval of the long-lost Rembrandt painting The Vision of Zacharias in the Temple (1633).
text: The Rijksmuseum is the national museum of the Netherlands dedicated to Dutch arts and history, located at the Museum Square in the borough of Amsterdam South, close to the Van Gogh Museum, the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam, and the Royal Concertgebouw. The Rijksmuseum was founded in The Hague on 19 November 1798 and moved to Amsterdam in 1808, where it was first located in the Royal Palace and later in the Trippenhuis.

title: Smiljan Radić is announced as the winner of the Pritzker Architecture Prize.
text: Smiljan Radić Clarke is a Chilean architect. His work includes residential buildings, cultural institutions, and temporary installations.

title: The Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA) opens its new David Geffen galleries designed by architect Peter Zumthor, to exhibit its permanent collection.
text: The Los Angeles County Museum of Art is an art museum located on Wilshire Boulevard in the Miracle Mile vicinity of Los Angeles. LACMA is on Museum Row, adjacent to the La Brea Tar Pits (George C. Page Museum).
wiki: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
